fragments.text: Both give 655 . They re anagrams same letters, same sum. Two different keys landing in the same bucket is a collision .

slide_text: How a dict works inside: Hash the key to a bucket index one arithmetic step Go directly to that bucket Collisions: each bucket keeps a short list to check That s why takes the same time whether the dict holds ten keys or ten million. This is called O(1) constant time.

fragments.text: Same idea at scale: a website splits a billion users across servers. Which server holds user 12345? . That s sharding .
If you add an 8th server, becomes almost every user is now on the wrong server. Real systems use smarter techniques (consistent hashing) to avoid reshuffling everyone.

slide_text: Quick Check: Two different keys hash to the same bucket (a collision). What happens? A. The second key silently replaces the first B. Python raises an error C. The bucket stores both pairs and lookup checks each one still fast if collisions are rare D. The hash function picks a different bucket

fragments.text: Answer: C. Each bucket keeps a short list of all key-value pairs that landed there. As long as the hash spreads keys evenly, the lists stay tiny and lookups remain fast.
